stem: Let $A$ be the set of all functions $f:\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Z$ and $R$ be a relation on $A$ such that $R=\{(f,g):f(0)=g(1)\text{ and }f(1)=g(0)\}$. Then $R$ is :

options.A: Symmetric and transitive but not reflexive
options.B: Symmetric but neither reflexive nor transitive
options.C: Reflexive but neither symmetric nor transitive
options.D: Transitive but neither reflexive nor symmetric

concepts: Properties of a relation on functions

steps.text: Reflexive needs $f(0)=f(1)$ for every $f$, which fails (e.g. $f(x)=x$).
Symmetric: $(f,g)\in R$ means $f(0)=g(1),\ f(1)=g(0)$, which is exactly the condition for $(g,f)\in R$.
Transitive: $(f,g),(g,h)\in R$ give $f(0)=g(1)=h(0)$, but transitivity needs $f(0)=h(1)$. Counterexample: $f=h=\text{id}$ and $g$ with $g(1)=0$, $g(0)=1$ gives $(f,g),(g,f)\in R$ but $(f,f)\notin R$.

pitfalls: Assuming $f(0)=f(1)$.

Limit $=\frac{\alpha}{-4/3}=3$ gives $\alpha=-4$. So $\beta+\gamma-\alpha=2+1+4=7$.
